description: A state matrix artifact is valid when every data-dependent screen declares all required states (loading, success, empty, error), error states have recovery actions, network-dependent screens have offline handling, and protected screens have unauthorized handling.

rules.description: state-matrix-spec.json must contain a non-empty screens array with at least one screen declared.
Every screen must have an id (string, non-empty) and a dataDependencies array.
Every screen with at least one data dependency must declare: loading, success, empty, and error states. These four are the minimum coverage for any data surface.
Every error, offline, unauthorized, or partial state must declare at least one recovery action (retry, redirect, recoveryActions array) or be explicitly marked terminal: true.
Screens with network-dependent data must declare an 'offline' state, or set offlineHandledGlobally: true. Missing offline coverage leaves users with no feedback when connectivity drops.
Auth-protected screens must declare an 'unauthorized' state to handle mid-session auth expiry, or set unauthorizedHandledByGuard: true.
Screens with paginated or optional data must declare a 'partial' state for when some but not all data has loaded.
Within a single screen, each state type (loading, error, empty, etc.) must appear at most once. Duplicates create ambiguity about which state definition applies.
State entries that are objects must declare a 'type' field. Typeless state objects cannot be validated by downstream compilers.
All screen ids must be unique within the state matrix. Duplicate ids cause ambiguous state lookups.
state-matrix-spec.json must declare a version string for change tracking.
No TODO, FIXME, HACK, or TBD in any spec file. These markers indicate incomplete state coverage which will propagate to implemented components.
